why: No hyperscaler has cut 2027 plans, but the risk has shifted to politics: after the Democratic sweep, UBS says ~30% of expected 2028 US data-centre additions could be at risk from construction pauses, and Microsoft is reportedly tightening oversight of neocloud projects. Spending is still debt-funded, with free cash flow negative at three of the four biggest spenders. New on Tue: momentum for a US plan to block imports of Chinese data-centre equipment, which Amazon, Alphabet and Meta oppose.

The chip index fell 5.3% on Mon and its 2026 gain has shrunk from ~106% in June to ~34%. Nvidia is ~24% down this month after Jensen Huang’s exit; the board is reportedly not discussing his return. Its results, the first under interim CEO Colette Kress, are due Tue after the US close (Wed ~8:20am Melbourne). Options priced a move of about 8% either way.

A 25 bp hike on 9 Dec is ~95% priced, with at least three hikes priced through 2027. Officials increasingly cite stubborn inflation; Chair Warsh says AI will have a ‘significant impact’ on the economy. October minutes due Wed.

Oracle −5% and CoreWeave −6% on Mon. Oracle is ~34% down in 2026, has ~US$108bn of debt and faces a bondholder lawsuit over borrowing disclosures; its default protection is reported near 300 bp. No newer CoreWeave level since 1,268 bp (5 Nov).

Anthropic prices its IPO on Wed 18 Nov (US time), aiming to raise up to ~US$80bn at close to a US$1.5tn valuation, and starts trading on Nasdaq on Thu as ANT. Its reception, in a falling market, is a direct test of appetite for the AI loop. (Disclosure: Claude is made by Anthropic.)
Eased to 5.12% on Mon and ~5.09% on Tue as investors bought bonds during the sell-off: a small flight-to-safety signal, but yields are still near their highest since 2002.
WTI fell 3.2% to US$85.72 on Mon as Hormuz flows recovered, although Iran reported at least four tankers hit by mines. Lower oil eases the inflation pressure behind Fed hikes.
High-yield spread tightened to 320 bp on 12 Nov (from 330 bp); investment grade 89 bp. Broad credit is calm. IMF: US bank loans to non-bank lenders rose 18% in 2026.

This is no longer just tech: on Mon 355 of 500 S&P stocks fell, the equal-weight index fell 1.0% and small caps 1.7%. On Tue NYSE decliners outnumbered advancers 3.25 to 1, with software, airlines and banks lagging. Broad selling is one of the ‘bursting’ signals.
